key_findings.finding: The remaining choices are less likely: C. difficile usually follows recent antibiotic or healthcare exposure; V. parahaemolyticus follows raw shellfish/seawater and is usually watery; Entamoeba histolytica causes dysentery but is generally more prolonged/travel-associated; Cryptosporidium and Giardia cause predominantly watery diarrhea (often prolonged, with Giardia causing malabsorption/bloating); Shigella can cause fever, tenesmus, and bloody diarrhea but is more strongly associated with person-to-person/fecal-contaminated food or water; Salmonella generally causes fever with inflammatory diarrhea; and Yersinia is linked to pork and pseudoappendicitis/terminal ileitis.
